objective: Produce a complete size-major Cartesian product without trimming or removing repeated pairs.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Nested traversal and flatMap remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Product option combinations are a practical pair-generation task.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Output order, multiplicity and dimension-based cost transfer.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Bounded string lengths make per-label work explicit.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Preserving literal values avoids modest display-data loss.

defects: Deduplication, trimming and post-computation source mutation all passed old distinct nonempty fixtures.
String domains, label construction cost and result freshness were implicit.
rationale: Specify dense bounded string lists, literal spaces/empties, multiplicity, size-major order, frozen input and fresh empty output. The exact count is the two-length product, bounded by n² for n equal to their maximum; bounded text length justifies constant work per pair. A reduce/concat trial was replaced by a fresh-array callback alternative to avoid repeated copying of a growing result. All three revealed variants and the final independent alternative pass the target/reward probe.

objective: Mutate only existing item prices with exact bounded half-cent rounding and no return value.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: forEach, Number arithmetic and Math.round remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Rounding integer-cent prices is a concrete transformation.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Mutation boundaries, aliasing and arithmetic order transfer.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Bounded integer cents and integer percentages define one assessable policy.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Half-cent revealed-answer errors can produce incorrect prices.

defects: The junior pre-divided factor and senior 1-percent/100 form could round a half cent down incorrectly.
Replacing item objects instead of changing their prices passed old value-only cases.
Percent and price domains, retained references and frozen outer arrays were unspecified.
rationale: Use distinct writable item objects, integer cents/percent bounds and the explicitly ordered Math.round(price*(100-percent)/100) formula. The product stays exact before division. An actual intermediate worker run rejected junior and senior on new half-cent fixtures while reference passed; both are corrected. Tests preserve item/metadata identities in a frozen outer array, other fields, full-discount boundary and undefined return. This is an educational pricing transformation, not a change to real billing.
